title: The Wedding People
author: Alison Espach
description: An unexpected arrival at a seaside hotel becomes part of a wedding weekend she never planned to attend. A warm, searching novel about unlikely friendship, imperfect beginnings and the possibilities that appear when a life changes direction.

title: James
author: Percival Everett
description: A familiar river journey is seen through a different pair of eyes. Everett gives Jim the centre of the story in a compelling novel about language, identity and the imagination required to claim a life of one’s own.

title: Erasure
author: Percival Everett
description: A novelist responds to the publishing world with a book he never expected anyone to take seriously. A sharp, inventive satire that asks who gets to tell a story, and what an audience expects to hear.

title: The Midnight Library
author: Matt Haig
description: Between one life and the next stands a library full of different possibilities. Nora explores the paths she might have taken in a thoughtful story about regret, connection and finding a reason to begin again.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
description: A man wakes alone on a spacecraft with a mission he cannot remember. Scientific puzzles and an unexpected friendship turn a journey through space into a story about resourcefulness, trust and working together.

title: The Alchemist
author: Paulo Coelho
description: A young shepherd leaves a familiar life to follow a recurring dream. His journey becomes a quiet invitation to notice the people, choices and small discoveries that give an adventure its meaning.

title: The Book Thief
author: Markus Zusak
description: In a German town during the Second World War, a young girl finds companionship in words and the people who share them. A moving novel about stories, courage and the fragile shelter of friendship.

title: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
description: A celebrated actor chooses an unexpected journalist to tell the story of her life. Behind the public image is a complicated portrait of ambition, loyalty, love and the cost of deciding what the world is allowed to know.

title: Tomorrow, and Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
author: Gabrielle Zevin
description: Two friends begin making games together, building imagined worlds while trying to understand the real one. A generous novel about creative work, lasting connection and the many ways a friendship can change.

title: Lessons in Chemistry
author: Bonnie Garmus
description: A determined chemist finds herself explaining far more than recipes on television. An energetic story about curiosity, independence and making room for a different kind of voice in a world with narrow expectations.

title: The Silent Patient
author: Alex Michaelides
description: A painter stops speaking after a shocking crime, and a therapist becomes determined to understand her silence. An intricate psychological mystery that keeps asking how much of another person’s story we can truly know.

title: The House in the Cerulean Sea
author: TJ Klune
description: An unassuming caseworker visits an unusual island home and finds his careful rules beginning to shift. A hopeful fantasy about belonging, kindness and the courage it can take to see people differently.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
description: An introduction to some of the largest questions in physics, from the beginning of the universe to the nature of black holes. A companion for curious readers who want to think beyond the everyday sky.

title: Cosmos
author: Carl Sagan
description: Sagan connects the scale of the universe with the human desire to understand it. Astronomy, the history of ideas and our place on a small planet come together in a wide-ranging invitation to stay curious.

title: Astrophysics for People in a Hurry
author: Neil deGrasse Tyson
description: Short chapters introduce the questions and discoveries that shape our understanding of the cosmos. A compact way to spend a little time with galaxies, gravity and the building blocks of the universe.

title: Sapiens
author: Yuval Noah Harari
description: A broad account of how human societies developed shared stories, institutions and ways of living. A provocative starting point for readers who enjoy asking how the past continues to shape the present.

title: The Silk Roads
author: Peter Frankopan
description: Trade routes become a way to see history from a different centre. Frankopan follows the movement of people, goods and ideas across the regions that have connected cultures for centuries.

title: The Diary of a Young Girl
author: Anne Frank
description: A young person’s observations of family, growing up and life in hiding become an enduring historical record. An intimate, thoughtful voice that invites careful reading and reflection on the world around it.

title: The Wild Robot
author: Peter Brown
description: A robot wakes on an island and must learn how to live among its animals. An imaginative adventure about adaptation, friendship and finding a place in a world that at first feels unfamiliar.

title: Wonder
author: R. J. Palacio
description: Starting a new school is a big step for Auggie and the people around him. Told through several perspectives, this story explores friendship, kindness and how a community learns to look beyond first impressions.

title: The Little Prince
author: Antoine de Saint-Exupéry
description: A traveller from a tiny planet shares his encounters with the grown-up world. A gentle, imaginative tale that leaves room for questions about friendship, responsibility and the things that matter most.

title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone
author: J. K. Rowling
description: A letter opens the door to a school unlike any Harry has known. His first year brings unexpected friendships, magical discoveries and a mystery at the heart of a world he is only beginning to understand.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
description: A practical exploration of how small routines become part of daily life. Clear examines the cues, environments and repeated choices that can make a habit easier to begin and easier to keep.

title: The Creative Act
author: Rick Rubin
description: Short reflections invite readers to notice more closely and make space for creative work. Rather than a single method, Rubin offers a collection of ways to think about attention, practice and the act of making.

title: The Psychology of Money
author: Morgan Housel
description: Stories about decision-making explore the human side of money: expectations, patience, uncertainty and the experiences people bring to a choice. A readable starting point for thinking about behaviour rather than just numbers.

title: The Mountain Is You
author: Brianna Wiest
description: A reflective look at the habits and inner conflicts that can make change feel difficult. Wiest invites readers to notice recurring patterns and consider how a different response might open a more useful way forward.
